art_instructions: Set the composition at eye level with the open front door of the cottage dividing the image: the left third shows the warm wooden interior, the right two thirds show the sunny exterior garden. In the doorway, Owl (round amber eyes, mottled brown-and-cream feathers, small green scarf) is mid-step leaving the house, one talon on the porch plank outside and the other still inside, wings slightly spread for balance. She wears her tiny satchel across her body as if heading out, and her head tilts toward the light with an eager, cheerful expression. Scale her at about half the door’s height, centered slightly right of the jamb so her body clearly crosses the threshold. Inside, show honey-brown wood walls and floor, a cream curtain by the door, and a small woven basket and potted green plant near the sill; the interior light is softer and warmer. Outside, show creamy white house walls with a sage-green shutter, a hint of terracotta roof edge, a small wooden porch with two steps down to a cobblestone path leading right, and a tidy garden of sunflowers and lavender. Bright sunlight streams in and casts Owl’s shadow onto the porch, emphasizing her direction from interior to exterior; a tiny butterfly near the sunflowers can add life but should stay small and secondary. If desired, include a subtle curved motion line from inside toward the path to make the action of leaving extra clear for young readers.
